title: Analytical Engine
brief: An 1843 workshop with the Analytical Engine, drawn entirely as a Victorian copperplate ENGRAVING: sepia-black ink on cream paper, tone made only from fine parallel hatching and cross-hatching (dense hatching = dark), engraved contour lines, a plate-mark border around the picture, a caption plate under it like a book illustration. Arched workshop windows, a big brass Engine on the right half: columns of stacked figure wheels (the 'store'), gear trains, a chain of punched cards. The first ~0.8 s of the scene (s.now < 0.8) the picture ENGRAVES ITSELF: hatching revealed line by line by a sweeping mask, then stays. ACTION: Jolly turns the big brass crank one full turn (crank wheel ~150 px, its handle in her lead mitten, the handle travelling a full circle during the action); the gears mesh and turn, a punched card advances along the chain, a small bell rings at the end (bell swings).
style: characterStyle tint sepia (#7a5a32, tintAlpha ~0.35) plus a light treat that overlays fine diagonal hatch lines source-atop at low alpha, so she reads as engraved but still cream.
portal: PUSH portal 'wheels': the grid of figure wheels on the Engine (rect, about 300×200 px, framed in brass), with s.peek('wheels') inside showing the next world; the Engine's numbers become the next machine's lamps.
sfx: tick on each quarter of the crank, chime when the bell rings

title: Electronic computer
brief: A 1946 computer room as a BLACK-AND-WHITE NEWSREEL: soft film grain (cached tiles, stepped), gentle vignette, faint vertical scratches and dust (stepped, subtle, never flickery), slightly lifted blacks. A wall of computer panels with rows of small lamps, plugboards with patch cables, round meters with needles, a big glowing VACUUM TUBE in a glass socket (~200×280 px) on a stand to the right. A newsreel title card at the top: 'THE MIGHTY ELECTRONIC BRAIN' in a period serif on a banner (it stays on screen, it is part of the set, not a cut). ACTION: Jolly plugs a patch cable (held in her mitten, a thick cable curving down to the floor) into a socket on the plugboard; the vacuum tube flares bright and the panel lamps cascade on, row by row, needles swing.
style: treat: grayscale + slight contrast (g.filter = 'grayscale(1) contrast(1.1) brightness(1.02)'), so she is a soft grey plush on film.
portal: PUSH portal 'tube': the glowing vacuum tube's glass envelope (rounded rect r≈60 or a tall rect ~170×240), with s.peek('tube') inside; glow 'rgba(255,240,200,.8)'. The switching moves into the next machine.
sfx: click when the plug goes in, thump when the tube flares

title: Mainframes
brief: A 1969 machine room in MID-CENTURY CUT PAPER: flat layered paper shapes with soft drop shadows between layers and a subtle paper texture, palette mustard #E3A92E, teal #1F7A7A, tomato #E0533B, cream #F3E9D2, charcoal #2B2B2B. Tall tape units with two big reels each (reels turning slowly, faster after the action), a processor panel with square lamps, a teletype printing paper that curls out. A CARD READER on the right (a desk-height cabinet with a card hopper and a clearly visible horizontal card SLOT). ACTION: Jolly feeds a punched card (cream card with holes, held in her mitten) into the reader; the card slides in, the tape reels spin up, the teletype prints a few lines and the paper curls out further.
style: characterStyle tint warm cream (#F3E9D2, tintAlpha 0.2) and a treat that posterises lightly (draw it at reduced saturation and add a 3px charcoal outline glow source-over behind via shadowBlur) so she looks like a paper cut-out.
portal: PUSH portal 'slot': the card reader's slot opening, made big and clearly framed (rect about 300×150 px, dark inside with a warm glow), with s.peek('slot') inside showing the next world; we follow the program in.
sfx: click when the card goes in, tick tick from the teletype

title: Home computers
brief: 1983 in 8-BIT PIXEL ART at dusk: everything drawn on a coarse pixel grid (draw the cached background at 1/6 size and scale up without smoothing, or draw in 6-px blocks), limited palette, sky banded from teal to amber, a few pixel stars. The LANDSCAPE IS A GIANT HOME COMPUTER: its keyboard keys are terraces Jolly stands on, a giant CRT monitor sits like a building on the right showing a BASIC program being typed line by line (driven by s.now, cursor blinking), a floppy drive slot set into a hillside above her head, and a 'DISKS' counter on a pixel sign. ACTION: Jolly jumps (lift) and bumps the floppy drive overhead with her mitten; a floppy pops out, arcs through the air and lands on the 'DISKS' counter, which ticks up by one.
style: treat: const o = U.pixelate(img, 7); o.pixel = true; return o;  plus a very light warm tint (characterStyle tint '#ffd9a0', tintAlpha 0.15).
portal: PUSH portal 'crt': the giant CRT's screen (rect ~400×300, r ~30, curved-glass look, bright bezel), s.peek('crt') inside; glow 'rgba(120,255,200,.7)'. Home computers lived on the TV.
sfx: thump on the bump, pop when the floppy pops out, beep when the counter ticks

title: The web
brief: 1996: a PERSONAL HOME PAGE AS A WORLD. Jolly stands inside a giant generic early web page: grey background with a tiled pattern, bevelled grey 3D buttons, blue underlined serif links, a spinning wireframe globe GIF-style (stepped animation at 8 fps), a scrolling marquee 'Welcome to my home page!' (driven by s.now), an 'under construction' stripe sign, a visitor counter with odometer digits, a horizontal rule, and a dial-up connection dialog box (grey window with a title bar, a 'Connect' button and a progress bar). Big 'ENTER' link text on the ground in front of her. Everything generic and invented: no real browser, OS or company. ACTION: Jolly presses the dial-up dialog's 'Connect' button (it depresses), the progress bar fills while the modem chirps, the visitor counter ticks up, then she hops (lift) over the 'ENTER' link which lights up.
style: characterStyle tint '#d8d8ff' tintAlpha 0.12 (a slight screen cast); no pixel pass.
portal: No portal of your own: the next scene (2007 showroom) PULLS back to reveal this page was on a phone screen. Keep the page animating until the end. Make sure the Connect button is the hotspot.
sfx: click on Connect, beep beep for the modem, pop on the hop

title: Smartphones
brief: 2007: a GLOSSY WHITE SHOWROOM: white walls, soft gradients, a reflective floor (reflections of the plinths), glass vitrines, little gel-bubble signs (glossy rounded labels). GENERIC SLAB PHONES (black glass, rounded corners, a single round home button, no logos) stand on white plinths. On the LEFT, a big phone on a plinth (its screen is the pull portal: Jolly steps out of it at the start, it then shows a soft generic home screen of plain rounded squares in pastel colours, or s.peek('phone') for a still of the web page). In front of the centre, a tall FROSTED GLASS PANE on a rail. On the RIGHT, a TABLET on a stand. Spotlights in the ceiling, off at first. ACTION: Jolly pushes the frosted pane aside (it slides right on its rail along with her mitten); the spotlights snap on one after another (cones of light fade in quickly but smoothly over ~0.15 s each), the tablet wakes up.
style: no tint; maybe a soft glossy highlight: characterStyle {} (keep her natural cream).
portal: TWO portals. 'phone' (the PULL portal: the phone screen on the left, about 200×356 portrait, r≈24, its bottom edge at floor level − ~40 so she can step out of it; its cover width = 356·16/9 ≈ 633: keep h ≤ 340). And 'tablet' (PUSH portal: the tablet screen on the right, about 420×300, r≈20, glow 'rgba(255,255,255,.6)', s.peek('tablet') inside; the screen became the computer). Put act.at about 380 px right of the phone's centre so she steps out and walks to the pane.
sfx: click when she grabs the pane, chime when the spotlights snap on

title: Attention
brief: 2017: a LAB WHITEBOARD filling the frame, drawn in BLACK MARKER with ONE ORANGE accent (#F56A2B); slightly uneven hand-drawn strokes, faint ghosts of erased writing, a marker tray at the bottom edge with markers, a few yellow sticky notes (the only other colour, pale). The sentence 'the cat napped because ___ was tired' written large across the board (marker lettering, consistent stroke), a small self-attention grid diagram (a square matrix of shaded cells) in a corner, sticky notes. ACTION: Jolly writes 'it' in the blank (the letters appear stroke by stroke as her mitten moves, as if she holds the marker) and circles it in orange; then attention arcs spring from 'it' to every word of the sentence, line thickness = attention weight, the heaviest and orange one landing on 'cat'.
style: characterStyle tint '#ffffff' tintAlpha 0.08 (stay natural, she is on a bright board).
portal: PUSH portal 'circle': the ORANGE CIRCLE around 'it', shape:'circle', about 240–300 px diameter (so make the written 'it' large), s.peek('circle') inside once it is drawn (fade the peek in as the circle closes); attention is where the model looks next.
sfx: tick tick as she writes, chime when the arcs spring

title: GPU clusters
brief: 2026: an ISOMETRIC FLAT-VECTOR DATACENTER: clean isometric racks of GPU servers in rows receding diagonally, palette copper #B8733A, graphite #2E3136, amber #F2A93B, with small amber status LEDs breathing (s.now), fans turning, cable trays overhead, a glowing TOKEN CONVEYOR BELT running along the floor in front with little rounded token tiles moving along it (s.now), and a big lever labelled 'TOKENS' on a pedestal. ACTION: Jolly pulls the TOKENS lever down (mitten on its handle); a wave of amber light runs across all the racks (LEDs light up in a travelling wave), the belt speeds up, and she hops onto the belt and rides it a little way to the right (use act.path dx up to +300 px, keep act.at + dx < 1400, with dy so she stands on the belt top).
style: characterStyle tint '#F2A93B' tintAlpha 0.12 (warm amber cast); no pixel pass.
portal: No portal of your own: the next scene PULLS back to reveal this datacenter was on the laptop screen in the finale. Keep everything animating until the end.
sfx: thump when the lever drops, tick ticks of the belt

title: Muse Spark on Fireworks
brief: NOW: a WARM DUSK ROOM. Palette: warm neutrals #F4F0EC and #121212 with Fireworks colours Glow #F56A2B, Flare #FB2D74, Bloom #7A155C, Plum #F0ACD6 (no blue-purple gradients, no neon violet). A big window (at least 1000×520) over a city skyline at dusk (warm charcoal sky warming to amber at the horizon, warm window lights in the buildings), a desk across the bottom of the frame (its top surface is the floor Jolly stands on), a desk lamp with a warm pool of light, a plant. A generic LAPTOP open on the desk (dark aluminium, no logo, a plain warm text field UI on its screen). At the start Jolly STEPS OUT OF THE LAPTOP SCREEN (the runtime does this, the screen is the pull portal) onto the desk and walks to her mark beside it. ACTION (s.u from 0 to 7.4, then the film holds 3.4 s more while s.u keeps increasing; keep everything driven by s.u so it holds still at the end): 0.0–1.4 the laptop types 'light up the sky?' (letters appear one by one, cursor blink); 1.4–3.0 it answers 'On it… 3… 2… 1…' (each count lands on a beat); 3.0–3.8 Jolly reaches and CLOSES THE LID (the lid rotates down onto the base, the screen light goes out); 3.8–6.0 FIREWORKS burst over the city outside the window: 6–9 big bursts (radius 120–260 px) with bright cores, sparkle trails, gravity droop, additive glow ('lighter'), in Glow/Flare/Plum with Bloom halos, the room flashing warm; 6.0–7.4 the sparks settle into the words 'Muse Spark' (large elegant serif, luminous) with 'now on Fireworks' below (smaller), sampled from text drawn on an offscreen canvas, inside the window; and a 'fireworks.ai' sign (a lit sign on the wall or in the window frame, ~44 px text, glowing border) lights up. After s.u = 7.4 everything holds steady and readable (only a gentle shimmer) until the fade. Jolly turns to look at the sky and gives a small wave.
style: characterStyle {} (her natural cream; the room light can warm her: tint '#F56A2B' tintAlpha 0.08).
portal: ONE portal: 'laptop' (the PULL portal: the laptop SCREEN, about 360×225 px, r≈8, on the desk near the centre; the previous scene (the datacenter) is shown in it during the pull, and Jolly steps out of its bottom edge onto the desk). Its rect must stay exactly where the open screen is drawn. After the pull, draw your own laptop UI in it. Put act.at about 260–380 px left of the laptop's centre so she stands beside it and the screen text is never hidden behind her; she reaches right to close the lid.
sfx: tick for typing (a few), beep on each count 3, 2, 1, thump when the lid closes, chime when the words form
